title: Light upon light
hookLine: His light is like a niche with a lamp in glass like a shining star, lit from a blessed olive (24:35)
carry: neither of the east nor of the west

lines: A CLAY LAMP IN OLIVE OIL.
cards: Before electricity, a house at night had one or two small lights, and people knew them intimately. A clay lamp with a wick floating in olive oil.

A little hollow cut into the wall to set it in, so the version wouldn't catch it and the plaster would throw the light back into the room. Glass, if you were lucky, to make the flame burn steady and bright.
Surah An-Nur, the Light, takes that ordinary lamp in the wall and uses it to describe something nobody can describe. Today, the Verse of Light.

teach.h: THE LIGHT OF THE HEAVENS AND EARTH.
teach.b: It begins with a sentence almost too large: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth." Then, straight away, it gets small.
The likeness of His light is a niche, a mishkat, and in it a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is like a shining star.
The lamp is lit from a blessed tree, an olive, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow on its own, even if no fire touched it.
Then the phrase this day is named for: "Light upon light."
The picture is built in layers, and each one gathers the light and makes it brighter, until the verse runs out of images and simply says it: light on top of light.
It ends by saying God guides to His light whom He wills, and sets out likenesses for people. It doesn't pretend the picture is the thing itself. It's a likeness, a way in.

Commentators have read the layers in many ways: the believer's heart as the niche, the Qur'an as the oil, the Prophet as the lamp. The theologian al-Ghazali wrote a book on this verse, called The Niche of Lights.
And the olive neither of the east nor of the west? Some say a tree standing in the open, catching sun all day. Others say it points beyond every direction.

how: The Verse of Light, 24:35, is often recited and often appears in Islamic calligraphy; some medieval mosque lamps were inscribed with it.

o: the niche in the wall where the lamp sits
the glass that shines like a star
the olive tree whose oil almost glows

games.q: the layers of the verse — tap the pairs.
p: neither of the east nor of the west

s: the verse says God's light is exactly a lamp
it calls the lamp a likeness, a way in, not the thing itself.
in the verse, the oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it
each layer gathers the light, until it is light upon light.
commentators all agree on what the niche stands for
they read it many ways: the heart, the Prophet, the Qur'an.

games.q: you need to describe the light of God in a single verse. what do you reach for?
o: a small lamp in a wall niche, behind glass.
games.why: the verse reaches for an ordinary household lamp, then layers niche, glass, star and oil until it says: light upon light.

practice: If you can, switch on a small lamp or light a candle somewhere safe, and turn off the brighter lights around it; if not, look at whatever light is nearest, a window, a screen dimmed low.
Watch how it falls on the wall behind it, and how the wall gives some of it back. If you pray, you can say the verse's opening line quietly.

wordCard.voice: Mishkat. The niche in the Verse of Light where the lamp sits, glowing through glass like a star.
